name: PainterOpt
comments:
PainterOpt sets the painter used to render the chart.
Each design system provides its own painter. If not set,
[DefaultPainter] is used.

name: PushValue
comments:
PushValue appends a data point to the named series. If the series has
reached MaxPoints, the oldest point is removed (rolling window).
Safe to call from any goroutine.

name: SeriesCount
comments: SeriesCount returns the number of series. Safe to call from any goroutine.

name: SeriesData
comments: SeriesData sets the initial static series data.

name: SeriesFn
comments:
SeriesFn sets a dynamic function that returns the current series data.
When set, this takes precedence over the static data but not over
a signal set via [SeriesSignal].

name: SeriesReadonlySignal
comments:
SeriesReadonlySignal binds the chart's series data to a read-only signal.
This is useful for computed signals. When set, this takes highest precedence.

name: SeriesSignal
comments:
SeriesSignal binds the chart's series data to a reactive signal.
This is a TWO-WAY binding: the widget reads series from the signal,
and when PushValue modifies series, the signal is updated.

name: ShowGrid
comments: ShowGrid enables or disables grid lines. Default is false.

name: ShowLabels
comments: ShowLabels enables or disables Y axis labels. Default is false.

name: Unmount
comments:
Unmount is called when the chart is removed from the widget tree.
Implements [widget.Lifecycle].

name: YRange
comments:
YRange sets the Y axis range [yMin, yMax].
Default is [0, 100].

name: DataPoint
comments: DataPoint represents a single data value in a series.

name: Series
comments: Series represents a named collection of data points with a display color.

name: Widget
comments:
Widget implements a real-time line chart for visualizing time-series data.

A line chart is created with [New] using functional options:

chart := linechart.New(
linechart.MaxPoints(60),
linechart.YRange(0, 100),
linechart.ShowGrid(true),
)

Data is pushed with [Widget.AddSeries] and [Widget.PushValue], which are
safe to call from any goroutine.

name: PaintChart
signature: func (DefaultPainter) (p DefaultPainter) PaintChart(canvas widget.Canvas, bounds geometry.Rect, cs PaintState)
comments:
PaintChart renders the chart with background, optional grid, optional labels,
and line segments for each data series.

name: PaintState
comments: PaintState holds the read-only snapshot passed to the painter.
code:
type PaintState struct {
	Series		[]Series
	MaxPoints	int
	YMin		float64
	YMax		float64
	ShowGrid	bool
	ShowLabels	bool
	GridColor	widget.Color
	Background	widget.Color
}

name: DefaultPainter
comments:
DefaultPainter provides a minimal fallback painter with no design system styling.
It draws background, grid lines, Y-axis labels, and line segments for each series.
code: type DefaultPainter struct{}

name: Painter
comments:
Painter renders the chart visuals.
Each design system (Material 3, Fluent, Cupertino) provides its own
Painter implementation to render the chart in its visual style.

If no Painter is set, [DefaultPainter] is used.

name: ResolvedDisabled
comments:
ResolvedDisabled returns the current disabled state.
Priority: ReadonlySignal > Signal > Fn > Static.

name: ResolvedItemCount
comments:
ResolvedItemCount returns the current item count.
Priority: ReadonlySignal > Signal > Fn > Static.

name: ResolvedSelectedIndex
comments:
ResolvedSelectedIndex returns the current selected index.
Priority: ReadonlySignal > Signal > Static.
Returns -1 if no selection.

name: String
comments: String returns a human-readable name for the selection mode.

name: ItemContext
comments:
ItemContext provides contextual information to the item builder callback.

The builder receives an ItemContext for each visible item, allowing it to
customize the returned widget based on selection, focus, and hover state.

name: A11yLabel
comments: A11yLabel sets the accessibility label for the list.

name: BuildItem
signature: func BuildItem(fn func(ctx ItemContext) widget.Widget) Option
comments:
BuildItem sets the callback that creates a widget for each visible item.
The callback receives an [ItemContext] with the item's index and state.
This is the primary convenience API for providing list content.

Internally, the function is wrapped into a [cdk.FuncContent] so that the
list view uniformly operates on [cdk.Content] for item rendering.

name: Disabled
comments: Disabled sets the list view's disabled state.

name: DisabledFn
comments:
DisabledFn sets a dynamic function for the disabled state.
When set, this takes precedence over [Disabled] but not over [DisabledSignal].

name: DisabledReadonlySignal
comments:
DisabledReadonlySignal binds the disabled state to a read-only signal.
When set, this takes highest precedence over all other disabled sources.

name: DisabledSignal
comments:
DisabledSignal binds the disabled state to a reactive signal.
When set, the signal takes precedence over [DisabledFn] and [Disabled]
but not over [DisabledReadonlySignal].

name: Divider
comments:
Divider enables drawing a divider between list items.
The divider is drawn by the [Painter].

name: EndReachedThreshold
comments:
EndReachedThreshold sets how many items from the end triggers [OnEndReached].
Default: 5 items.

name: EstimatedItemHeight
comments:
EstimatedItemHeight sets the estimated height for items that have not
been measured yet. Only used when neither [FixedItemHeight] nor
[ItemHeightFn] is set. Default: 48 pixels.

name: FixedItemHeight
comments:
FixedItemHeight sets a uniform height for all items.
This enables the O(1) fast path with no per-item measurement.
Mutually exclusive with [ItemHeightFn].

name: ItemContent
comments:
ItemContent sets the [cdk.Content] used to render each visible item.
This is the enterprise API for providing list content — use it when you
need reusable content implementations or progressive complexity
(string → function → widget).

For most use cases, [BuildItem] is simpler and sufficient.

name: ItemCount
comments: ItemCount sets the total number of items in the list.

name: ItemCountFn
comments:
ItemCountFn sets a dynamic function that returns the item count.
When set, this takes precedence over [ItemCount] but not over [ItemCountSignal].

name: ItemCountReadonlySignal
comments:
ItemCountReadonlySignal binds the item count to a read-only signal.
When set, this takes highest precedence over all other item count sources.

name: ItemCountSignal
comments:
ItemCountSignal binds the item count to a reactive signal.
When set, the signal takes precedence over [ItemCountFn] and [ItemCount]
but not over [ItemCountReadonlySignal].

name: ItemHeightFn
signature: func ItemHeightFn(fn func(index int) float32) Option
comments:
ItemHeightFn sets a callback that returns the height for the item at
the given index. Heights are cached after first call, enabling O(log n)
lookup via binary search on cumulative offsets.
Mutually exclusive with [FixedItemHeight].

name: OnEndReached
comments:
OnEndReached sets the callback invoked when the user scrolls near the
end of the list. Useful for infinite scroll / pagination.
The threshold is configurable via [EndReachedThreshold].

name: OnItemClick
comments: OnItemClick sets the callback invoked when an item is clicked.

name: OnScroll
comments: OnScroll sets the callback invoked when the scroll position changes.

name: OnSelectionChange
comments: OnSelectionChange sets the callback invoked when the selected item changes.

name: Overscan
comments:
Overscan sets the number of extra items to render above and below the
visible viewport. Higher values reduce blank flashes during fast scroll
at the cost of rendering more items. Default: 3 items.

name: PainterOpt
comments:
PainterOpt sets the painter used to render list-specific visuals.
Each design system provides its own painter. If not set,
[DefaultPainter] is used.

name: ScrollYSignal
comments:
ScrollYSignal binds the vertical scroll offset to a reactive signal.
This is a TWO-WAY binding passed through to the internal ScrollView.

name: SelectedIndex
comments:
SelectedIndex sets the initially selected item index.
Use -1 for no selection.

name: SelectedIndexReadonlySignal
comments:
SelectedIndexReadonlySignal binds the selected index to a read-only signal.
When set, this takes highest precedence over all other selection sources.

name: SelectedIndexSignal
comments:
SelectedIndexSignal binds the selected index to a reactive signal.
This is a TWO-WAY binding: the widget reads from the signal, and
when the user selects an item, the new index is written back.

name: SelectionModeOpt
comments:
SelectionModeOpt sets the selection mode for the list.
Default is [SelectionNone].

name: PaintDivider
signature: func (DefaultPainter) (p DefaultPainter) PaintDivider(canvas widget.Canvas, ds DividerState)
comments: PaintDivider draws a thin horizontal line at the divider bounds.

name: PaintEmptyState
signature: func (DefaultPainter) (p DefaultPainter) PaintEmptyState(canvas widget.Canvas, bounds geometry.Rect)
comments: PaintEmptyState draws a centered "No items" message.

name: PaintItemBackground
signature: func (DefaultPainter) (p DefaultPainter) PaintItemBackground(canvas widget.Canvas, ips ItemPaintState)
comments: PaintItemBackground draws the background for a list item.

name: PaintSelection
signature: func (DefaultPainter) (p DefaultPainter) PaintSelection(canvas widget.Canvas, ips ItemPaintState)
comments: PaintSelection draws the selection highlight for a selected item.

name: DividerState
comments: DividerState provides context for divider painting.

name: ItemPaintState
comments: ItemPaintState provides context for item background and selection painting.

name: ListColorScheme
comments:
ListColorScheme provides theme-derived colors for list painting.
Zero value means the painter should use its built-in defaults.
code:
type ListColorScheme struct {
	DividerColor		widget.Color	// divider line color
	SelectionColor		widget.Color	// selected item background
	HoverColor		widget.Color	// hovered item background
	FocusColor		widget.Color	// focused item border/background
	EmptyTextColor		widget.Color	// empty state text color
	ItemBackground		widget.Color	// alternating item background (even rows)
	ItemBackgroundAlt	widget.Color	// alternating item background (odd rows)
}

name: DefaultPainter
comments:
DefaultPainter provides a minimal fallback painter with no design system styling.
It draws simple list visuals -- useful for testing and as a base reference.
code: type DefaultPainter struct{}

name: Painter
comments:
Painter draws list-specific visual elements.
Each design system (Material 3, Fluent, Cupertino) provides its own
Painter implementation to render the list in its visual style.

If no Painter is set, the list view uses [DefaultPainter].

name: Children
comments:
Children returns the cached item widgets for dirty-region collection.
Their ScreenBounds (set during the previous Draw) allow the dirty.Collector to
report item-level dirty rects clipped to the viewport.

name: Draw
comments: Draw renders only the visible items within the current viewport.

name: Event
signature: func (*virtualContent) (vc *virtualContent) Event(ctx widget.Context, e event.Event) bool
comments: Event delegates events back to the parent list for item interaction.

name: Layout
signature: func (*virtualContent) (vc *virtualContent) Layout(_ widget.Context, c geometry.Constraints) geometry.Size
comments:
Layout returns the total content size: full viewport width and the sum of
all item heights (real or estimated). This tells the ScrollView how much
scrollable area exists.

name: AccessibilityActions
comments: AccessibilityActions returns the list of supported actions.

name: AccessibilityHint
comments: AccessibilityHint returns the accessibility hint.

name: AccessibilityLabel
comments: AccessibilityLabel returns the accessibility label.

name: AccessibilityRole
comments: AccessibilityRole returns the ARIA role for this widget.

name: AccessibilityState
comments: AccessibilityState returns the current accessibility state.

name: AccessibilityValue
comments: AccessibilityValue returns the current list state as a string.

name: Children
comments: Children returns the internal scroll view as the single child.

name: Draw
comments: Draw renders the list view to the canvas.

name: Event
signature: func (*Widget) (w *Widget) Event(ctx widget.Context, e event.Event) bool
comments: Event handles an input event and returns true if consumed.

name: GetItemCount
comments: GetItemCount returns the current item count.

name: InvalidateData
comments:
InvalidateData signals that the underlying data has changed.
This invalidates the widget cache and triggers re-layout.

name: IsFocusable
comments: IsFocusable reports whether the list view can currently receive focus.

name: Layout
signature: func (*Widget) (w *Widget) Layout(ctx widget.Context, constraints geometry.Constraints) geometry.Size
comments: Layout calculates the list view's size within the given constraints.

name: Mount
comments:
Mount creates signal bindings for push-based invalidation.
Implements [widget.Lifecycle].

name: New
comments:
New creates a new list view Widget with the given options.

The returned widget is visible, enabled, and focusable by default.
If no [BuildItem] callback is provided, the list renders empty.

name: ScrollToIndex
comments:
ScrollToIndex scrolls to make the item at the given index visible.
If the item is already fully visible, this is a no-op.

name: Unmount
comments:
Unmount is called when the list view is removed from the widget tree.
Implements [widget.Lifecycle].

name: VisibleRange
comments: VisibleRange returns the indices of currently visible items [start, end).

name: Widget
ContextPainterOpt
comments: ContextPainterOpt sets the painter used to render the context menu.

name: Hide
comments: Hide closes the context menu.

name: IsOpen
comments: IsOpen returns true if the context menu is currently visible.

name: Items
comments: Items returns the context menu items.

name: NewContextMenu
comments: NewContextMenu creates a new context menu with the given items and options.

name: Panel
comments:
Panel returns the active menu panel for testing. Returns nil when closed.
The returned value implements [widget.Widget] and [PanelState].

name: Show
comments:
Show opens the context menu at the given position via the overlay manager.
If the context menu is already open, it is closed first.

name: ContextMenu
comments:
ContextMenu is a floating popup menu shown at a specific position,
typically on right-click. It contains a list of menu items that the
user can select via mouse or keyboard.

Create with [NewContextMenu].

name: BarMenu
comments: BarMenu creates a TopMenu definition for use with NewBar.

name: HasChildren
comments: HasChildren reports whether this item has a submenu.

name: IsSeparator
comments: IsSeparator reports whether this item is a separator line.

name: Item
signature: func Item(label, shortcut string, onAction func()) MenuItem
comments:
Item creates a regular menu item with a label, shortcut display text,
and action callback.

name: ItemDisabled
comments: ItemDisabled creates a disabled menu item that cannot be activated.

name: Sep
comments: Sep creates a separator menu item displayed as a horizontal line.

name: SubMenu
comments: SubMenu creates a menu item that opens a nested submenu on hover.

name: MenuItem
comments:
MenuItem defines a single entry in a menu. It can be a regular action item,
a separator, or a submenu parent containing children.

name: TopMenu
comments:
TopMenu defines a top-level menu in a MenuBar. It has a label shown
in the bar and a list of items displayed in the dropdown.

name: Children
comments: Children returns nil; the menu is a leaf widget (submenus are overlays).

name: Draw
comments: Draw renders the menu panel.

name: Event
signature: func (*menuPanel) (m *menuPanel) Event(ctx widget.Context, e event.Event) bool
comments: Event handles input events for the popup menu.

name: HighlightedIndex
comments: HighlightedIndex returns the currently highlighted item index for testing.

name: Layout
signature: func (*menuPanel) (m *menuPanel) Layout(_ widget.Context, constraints geometry.Constraints) geometry.Size
comments: Layout returns the panel's preferred size.

name: SubMenuIndex
comments: SubMenuIndex returns the index of the item whose submenu is open for testing.

name: SubMenuPanel
comments: SubMenuPanel returns the open submenu panel for testing.

name: PanelState
comments:
PanelState is the exported interface for accessing menu panel state.
This is primarily used for testing.

name: A11yLabel
comments: A11yLabel returns the accessibility label.

name: A11yRole
comments: A11yRole returns the ARIA role for the menu bar.

name: Children
comments: Children returns nil; the menu bar is a leaf widget (menus are overlays).

name: Close
comments: Close closes any open menu.

name: Draw
comments: Draw renders the menu bar.

name: Event
signature: func (*Bar) (b *Bar) Event(ctx widget.Context, e event.Event) bool
comments: Event handles input events for the menu bar.

name: HoveredIndex
comments: HoveredIndex returns the index of the hovered label, or -1.

name: IsFocusable
comments: IsFocusable reports whether the menu bar can currently receive focus.

name: IsOpen
comments: IsOpen returns true if any top-level menu is currently open.

name: Layout
signature: func (*Bar) (b *Bar) Layout(_ widget.Context, constraints geometry.Constraints) geometry.Size
comments:
Layout calculates the menu bar's preferred size.
The bar occupies the full available width and a fixed height.

name: Menus
comments: Menus returns the top-level menu definitions.

name: NewBar
comments:
NewBar creates a new MenuBar widget with the given top-level menus and options.

The returned widget is visible and enabled by default.

name: OpenIndex
comments: OpenIndex returns the index of the currently open top-level menu, or -1.

name: PainterOpt
comments: PainterOpt sets the painter used to render the menu bar and its menus.

name: Bar
comments:
Bar is a horizontal menu bar widget displayed at the top of a window.
It contains top-level menu labels that open dropdown menus when clicked.

Bar follows the functional options pattern for construction.
Create with [NewBar].

name: PaintMenu
comments: PaintMenu renders a minimal popup menu panel.

name: PaintMenuBar
comments: PaintMenuBar renders a minimal menu bar.

name: MenuBarPaintState
comments: MenuBarPaintState provides the current menu bar state to the painter.

name: MenuPaintState
comments: MenuPaintState provides the current popup menu state to the painter.

name: MenuColorScheme
comments:
MenuColorScheme provides theme-derived colors for menu painting.
Zero value means the painter should use its built-in defaults.
code:
type MenuColorScheme struct {
	BarBackground		widget.Color
	BarText			widget.Color
	BarHover		widget.Color
	BarActiveText		widget.Color
	MenuBackground		widget.Color

name: DefaultPainter
comments:
DefaultPainter provides a minimal fallback painter for menus.
It draws simple rectangles and text without design system styling.

comments:
Painter draws the visual representation of menus and menu bars.
Each design system (Material 3, Fluent, Cupertino) provides its own
Painter implementation. If no Painter is set, [DefaultPainter] is used.

name: Content
comments: Content sets the widget displayed inside the popover.

name: ContentSize
comments:
ContentSize sets a fixed size for the popover content area.
If not set, the content widget's natural size is used.

name: Delay
comments:
Delay sets the hover delay before showing a tooltip. Defaults to 500ms.
Only applies to [Tooltip], not [Popover].

name: Disabled
comments: Disabled sets the popover's disabled state. Disabled popovers do not open.

name: DisabledFn
comments:
DisabledFn sets a dynamic function that determines whether the popover
is disabled. When set, this takes precedence over the static value.

name: DismissOnClickOutside
comments:
DismissOnClickOutside controls whether clicking outside the popover
content dismisses it. Defaults to true.

name: Gap
comments:
Gap sets the spacing between the trigger and the overlay in logical pixels.
Defaults to 4.

name: MaxWidth
comments:
MaxWidth sets the maximum width for tooltip text wrapping.
Defaults to 300 logical pixels.

name: OnHide
comments: OnHide sets a callback invoked when the popover or tooltip is hidden.

name: OnShow
comments: OnShow sets a callback invoked when the popover or tooltip becomes visible.

name: PainterOpt
comments: PainterOpt sets the painter used to render the popover or tooltip.

name: PlacementOpt
comments: PlacementOpt sets the preferred placement relative to the trigger.

name: ResolvedDisabled
comments:
ResolvedDisabled returns the current disabled state, preferring the
dynamic function over the static bool.

name: TooltipText
comments: TooltipText sets the text displayed in a tooltip.

name: TriggerWidget
comments: TriggerWidget sets the widget that anchors the popover/tooltip.

name: VisibleSignal
comments:
VisibleSignal binds the visible state to a reactive signal for two-way
data binding. When the signal is set externally, the popover shows/hides.

name: PaintPopover
comments: PaintPopover renders a popover background with shadow.

name: PaintTooltip
comments: PaintTooltip renders a tooltip background and text.

name: PopoverPaintState

name: TooltipPaintState
comments: TooltipPaintState provides the current tooltip state to the painter.

name: PopoverColorScheme
comments:
PopoverColorScheme provides theme-derived colors for popover painting.
Zero value means the painter should use its built-in defaults.

name: TooltipColorScheme
comments:
TooltipColorScheme provides theme-derived colors for tooltip painting.
Zero value means the painter should use its built-in defaults.

name: DefaultPainter
comments:
DefaultPainter provides a minimal fallback painter for popovers and
tooltips. It draws rounded rectangles with a subtle shadow.
code: type DefaultPainter struct{}

name: Painter
comments:
Painter draws the visual representation of popovers and tooltips.
Each design system (Material 3, Fluent, Cupertino) provides its own
Painter implementation. If no Painter is set, [DefaultPainter] is used.

name: CalculatePosition

func CalculatePosition(

	triggerBounds geometry.Rect,

	windowSize geometry.Size,

CalculatePosition computes the overlay position given the trigger bounds,
overlay size, and window size. It applies auto-flip logic when the overlay
would overflow the viewport, then clamps to the window bounds.

signature: func (*overlayContent) (oc *overlayContent) Event(ctx widget.Context, e event.Event) bool

name: SetBounds

name: Show

name: Toggle

name: Unmount
comments: Unmount is called when the popover is removed from the widget tree.

name: Popover
comments:
Popover is a click-triggered floating overlay that displays arbitrary widget
content anchored to a trigger widget. It integrates with the overlay stack
for z-ordering and supports click-outside dismissal.

name: Children
comments: Children returns nil; tooltip overlay is a leaf widget.

comments: Children returns the trigger widget as the sole child.

name: Draw

comments:
Draw renders the trigger widget. The tooltip content is drawn by the
overlay stack.

signature: func (*Tooltip) (t *Tooltip) Event(ctx widget.Context, e event.Event) bool
comments: Event handles input events, primarily mouse enter/leave on the trigger.

name: IsOpen

name: NewTooltip

name: Text

name: Tooltip
comments:

It appears after a configurable delay when the mouse enters the trigger,
and disappears when the mouse leaves.

Create with [NewTooltip] using functional options.

name: PaintProgress
signature: func (DefaultPainter) (p DefaultPainter) PaintProgress(canvas widget.Canvas, ps PaintState)
comments:
PaintProgress renders the circular progress indicator.
In determinate mode, it draws a track circle and a progress arc.
In indeterminate mode, it draws a rotating partial arc.

name: PaintState
comments: PaintState provides the current progress indicator state to the painter.
code:
type PaintState struct {
	Value		float64			// current value clamped to [0, 1] (determinate mode)
	Bounds		geometry.Rect		// total widget bounds
	Diameter	float32			// indicator diameter in logical pixels
	StrokeWidth	float32			// arc stroke width in logical pixels
	ShowLabel	bool			// whether to show percentage label (determinate only)
	Label		string			// pre-formatted label text (empty if ShowLabel is false)
	Indeterminate	bool			// true for spinner mode
	Rotation	float64			// current rotation in radians (indeterminate mode)
	AnimationPhase	float64			// 0-1 sawtooth phase within one grow/shrink cycle
	Disabled	bool			// widget is disabled
	ColorScheme	ProgressColorScheme	// theme-derived colors (zero = use defaults)
}

name: DefaultPainter
comments:
DefaultPainter provides a minimal fallback painter with no design system styling.
It draws a circular progress indicator using cubic Bézier arc strokes.
code: type DefaultPainter struct{}

name: Painter
comments:
Painter draws the visual representation of a circular progress indicator.
Each design system (Material 3, Fluent, Cupertino) provides its own
Painter implementation to render the indicator in its visual style.

If no Painter is set, the progress indicator uses [DefaultPainter].

name: Children
comments: Children returns nil because a progress indicator is a leaf widget.

name: ColorSchemeOpt
comments:
ColorSchemeOpt sets the full color scheme for painting.
This overrides the painter's built-in defaults.

name: Disabled
comments: Disabled sets the indicator's disabled state.

name: DisabledFn
comments:
DisabledFn sets a dynamic function for the disabled state.
When set, this takes precedence over the static value but not
over a signal set via [DisabledSignal].

name: DisabledReadonlySignal
comments:
DisabledReadonlySignal binds the disabled state to a read-only signal.
When set, this takes highest precedence over all other disabled sources.

name: DisabledSignal
comments:
DisabledSignal binds the disabled state to a reactive signal.
When set, the signal value takes precedence over both [DisabledFn]
and [Disabled] but not over [DisabledReadonlySignal].

name: Draw
comments: Draw renders the circular progress indicator to the canvas.

name: Event
comments:
Event handles an input event. Progress indicators are display-only and always
return false (events are never consumed).

name: FormatLabelFn
comments:
FormatLabelFn sets a custom label formatting function.
The function receives the current value (0.0 to 1.0) and returns
the label string. If nil, the default "65%" format is used.

name: Indeterminate
comments:
Indeterminate sets whether the indicator shows as a spinning arc.
When true, the value is ignored and the arc rotates continuously.

name: IndicatorColor
comments: IndicatorColor sets the progress arc color.

name: IsIndeterminate

func (w *Widget) Layout(_ widget.Context, constraints geometry.Constraints) geometry.Size {
	stripW := w.resolvedWidth()
	preferred := geometry.Sz(stripW, constraints.MaxHeight)
	size := constraints.Constrain(preferred)

	w.layoutButtons(size)
	w.SetBounds(geometry.FromPointSize(w.Position(), size))
	return size
}

name: Run
comments:
Run starts a desktop application with a per-boundary GPU texture render loop.

ADR-007 Phase 7: per-boundary GPU textures with damage-aware blit.

The rendering pipeline:
1. Frame() flushes signals, layouts, animations
2. PaintBoundaryLayers: re-record dirty+visible boundaries (Flutter flushPaint)
3. renderBoundaryTextures: per-boundary offscreen GPU textures (MSAA)
4. compositeTextures: blit all textures to surface (non-MSAA)
5. DrawOverlays + damage tracking + present

Run blocks until the window is closed.

name: DragData
comments:
DragData carries the payload during a drag operation.

Kind identifies the type of data being dragged (e.g., "text", "widget",
"file"). DropTargets use Kind to determine whether they can accept
the data without inspecting the payload.

comments: Feedback carries visual feedback information during an active drag.

name: DragSource
comments:
DragSource is implemented by widgets that can initiate drag operations.

Widgets implement this interface to participate as drag sources. The Manager
detects DragSource via type assertion when processing mouse press events.

name: DropTarget
comments:
DropTarget is implemented by widgets that can accept dropped data.

Widgets implement this interface to participate as drop targets. Targets
are registered with the Manager along with their bounds.

comments:
NewDragVisual creates a DragVisual from an active Session.

Returns a zero DragVisual if the session is nil or inactive.

name: DragVisual
comments:
DragVisual describes how to render drag feedback.

Applications can inspect the active Session and its Feedback to render
custom drag visuals (ghost widgets, drop indicators, etc.). This type
provides common visual parameters that painters can use.

name: Cancel
comments:
Cancel cancels the active drag operation, if any.

This is equivalent to the user pressing Escape during a drag.

name: CurrentSession
comments:
CurrentSession returns the active drag session, or nil if no drag is active.

The returned Session should not be stored beyond the current event cycle,
as it may be invalidated when the drag ends.

name: HandleKeyEvent
comments:
HandleKeyEvent processes a key event for drag cancellation.

Returns true if the event was consumed (Escape pressed during active drag).

name: HandleMouseEvent
comments:
HandleMouseEvent processes a mouse event for drag and drop.

Returns true if the event was consumed by drag/drop handling.
The source parameter is the widget under the cursor for drag initiation;
it may be nil if no DragSource is under the cursor.

name: IsDragging

name: RegisterTarget
comments:

If the target is already registered, its bounds are updated.

name: TargetCount
comments: TargetCount returns the number of registered drop targets.

name: UnregisterTarget
comments:
UnregisterTarget removes a DropTarget from the manager.

If the target is currently the hover target of an active drag, DragLeave
is called before removal.

name: UpdateTargetBounds
comments:
UpdateTargetBounds updates the bounds for a registered target.

This should be called after layout changes to keep hit testing accurate.

name: Manager
comments:
Manager coordinates drag and drop operations across the widget tree.

It handles the full drag lifecycle: detection (mouse press + threshold),
session management, target enter/over/leave dispatch, and drop/cancel.

Manager is safe for concurrent access. All exported methods are
protected by a mutex.

comments: CurrentPos returns the current cursor position during the drag.

name: CurrentTarget
comments: CurrentTarget returns the DropTarget currently under the cursor, or nil.

name: Data
comments: Data returns the drag data for this session.

name: Feedback
comments: Feedback returns the current visual feedback for the drag.

name: Source

name: StartPos

name: Session
comments:
Session represents an active drag operation.

A Session is created by the Manager when a drag is initiated (mouse press
on a DragSource followed by movement beyond the drag threshold). It tracks
the drag data, source widget, positions, and current hover target.

Session is not safe for concurrent access. It is managed exclusively
by the Manager, which provides its own synchronization.

comments: Has returns true if the specified button is pressed.

name: IsDoubleClick
comments: IsDoubleClick returns true if this is a double-click event.

name: IsDrag
comments: IsDrag returns true if this is a drag event.

name: IsEnter
comments: IsEnter returns true if this is a mouse enter event.

name: IsLeave
comments: IsLeave returns true if this is a mouse leave event.

name: IsLeftButton
comments: IsLeftButton returns true if the left button is involved.

name: IsLeftPressed
comments: IsLeftPressed returns true if the left button is pressed.

name: IsMiddleButton
comments: IsMiddleButton returns true if the middle button is involved.

name: IsMiddlePressed
comments: IsMiddlePressed returns true if the middle button is pressed.

name: IsMove
comments: IsMove returns true if this is a mouse move event.

name: IsPress
comments: IsPress returns true if this is a button press event.

name: IsRelease
comments: IsRelease returns true if this is a button release event.

name: IsRightButton
comments: IsRightButton returns true if the right button is involved.

name: IsRightPressed
comments: IsRightPressed returns true if the right button is pressed.

name: IsX1Pressed
comments: IsX1Pressed returns true if the X1 button is pressed.

name: IsX2Pressed
comments: IsX2Pressed returns true if the X2 button is pressed.

name: NewMouseEvent
signature:
func NewMouseEvent(
	mouseType MouseEventType,
	button Button,
	buttons ButtonState,
	position geometry.Point,
	globalPosition geometry.Point,
	mods Modifiers,
) *MouseEvent
comments: NewMouseEvent creates a new mouse event with the current time.

name: NewMouseEventWithTime
signature:
func NewMouseEventWithTime(
	mouseType MouseEventType,
	button Button,
	buttons ButtonState,
	position geometry.Point,
	globalPosition geometry.Point,
	mods Modifiers,
	t time.Time,
) *MouseEvent
comments: NewMouseEventWithTime creates a new mouse event with a specific timestamp.

name: String
comments: String returns a human-readable name for the mouse event type.
code:
func (t MouseEventType) String() string {
	switch t {
	case MousePress:
		return mousePressStr
	case MouseRelease:
		return mouseReleaseStr
	case MouseMove:
		return mouseMoveStr
	case MouseEnter:
		return mouseEnterStr
	case MouseLeave:
		return mouseLeaveStr
	case MouseDrag:
		return mouseDragStr
	case MouseDoubleClick:
		return mouseDoubleClickStr
	default:
		return unknownStr
	}
}

name: String
comments: String returns a human-readable name for the button.
code:
func (b Button) String() string {
	switch b {
	case ButtonNone:
		return buttonNoneStr
	case ButtonLeft:
		return buttonLeftStr
	case ButtonRight:
		return buttonRightStr
	case ButtonMiddle:
		return buttonMiddleStr
	case ButtonX1:
		return "X1"
	case ButtonX2:
		return "X2"
	default:
		return unknownStr
	}
}

name: String
comments: String returns a human-readable representation of the event.

name: MouseEvent
comments:
MouseEvent represents a mouse input event.

Position is relative to the widget receiving the event.
GlobalPosition is the position in screen coordinates.

name: DeltaX
comments: DeltaX returns the horizontal scroll amount.

name: DeltaY
comments: DeltaY returns the vertical scroll amount.

name: IsHorizontal
comments: IsHorizontal returns true if there is any horizontal scrolling.

name: IsScrollDown
comments: IsScrollDown returns true if scrolling down (negative Y delta).

name: IsScrollLeft
comments: IsScrollLeft returns true if scrolling left (negative X delta).

name: IsScrollRight
comments: IsScrollRight returns true if scrolling right (positive X delta).

name: IsScrollUp
comments: IsScrollUp returns true if scrolling up (positive Y delta).

name: IsVertical
comments: IsVertical returns true if there is any vertical scrolling.

name: NewWheelEvent
comments: NewWheelEvent creates a new wheel event with the current time.

name: NewWheelEventWithTime
signature:
func NewWheelEventWithTime(
	delta geometry.Point,
	position geometry.Point,
	globalPosition geometry.Point,
	mods Modifiers,
	t time.Time,
) *WheelEvent
comments: NewWheelEventWithTime creates a new wheel event with a specific timestamp.

name: String
comments: String returns a human-readable representation of the event.

name: WheelEvent
comments:
WheelEvent represents a mouse wheel scroll event.

Delta contains the scroll amount in both directions.
The sign convention matches the gogpu platform:
- Positive Delta.Y means scrolling down (content moves up)
- Negative Delta.Y means scrolling up (content moves down)
- Positive Delta.X means scrolling right
- Negative Delta.X means scrolling left

The delta values are typically in "lines" for discrete scroll wheels,
or pixels for smooth scrolling (e.g., trackpads).

name: Frame
comments: Frame carries a rendered module image to the compositor.

name: Blur
comments:
Blur removes focus from the currently focused widget.

After calling Blur, [Manager.Focused] returns nil.

name: DrawFocusRing
signature: func DrawFocusRing(canvas widget.Canvas, bounds geometry.Rect, color widget.Color, radius float32)
comments:
DrawFocusRing draws a focus indicator around the given bounds.

The ring is drawn as a rounded rectangle outline, offset slightly
outside the bounds. The radius controls corner rounding; use 0 for
square corners.

Example:

if w.IsFocused() {
focus.DrawFocusRing(canvas, w.Bounds(), widget.ColorBlue, 4.0)
}

name: Focus
comments:
Focus sets keyboard focus to the given widget.

If another widget currently has focus, it is blurred first.
If w is nil, focus is cleared (equivalent to [Manager.Blur]).
If w is not focusable (IsFocusable returns false), this is a no-op.

name: Focused
comments: Focused returns the currently focused widget, or nil if no widget has focus.

name: HandleKeyEvent
comments:
HandleKeyEvent processes a key event for focus management.

The event is checked in the following order:
1. Registered keyboard shortcuts
2. Tab key (moves focus to next widget)
3. Shift+Tab (moves focus to previous widget)

Returns true if the event was consumed (shortcut matched or tab navigation
occurred), false otherwise.

name: New
comments:
New creates a new focus [Manager] for the given widget tree root.

The root widget is the top-level widget whose subtree will be
traversed for focus management. It may be nil, in which case the
manager operates as a no-op until SetRoot is called.

name: Next
comments:
Next moves focus to the next focusable widget in tab order.

Tab order is determined by depth-first traversal of the widget tree.
If no widget currently has focus, focus moves to the first focusable widget.
If the last focusable widget has focus, focus wraps to the first.
If no focusable widgets exist, this is a no-op.

name: Previous
comments:
Previous moves focus to the previous focusable widget in tab order.

If no widget currently has focus, focus moves to the last focusable widget.
If the first focusable widget has focus, focus wraps to the last.
If no focusable widgets exist, this is a no-op.

name: RegisterShortcut
comments:
RegisterShortcut registers a global keyboard shortcut.

When the shortcut's key combination is pressed, the handler function
is called. Shortcuts take precedence over tab navigation.

name: SetRoot
comments:
SetRoot replaces the widget tree root.

If the currently focused widget is no longer in the new tree,
focus is cleared.

name: UnregisterShortcut
comments: UnregisterShortcut removes all handlers for the given shortcut.

name: Manager
comments:
Manager tracks keyboard focus within a widget tree.

It maintains a reference to the widget tree root and the currently
focused widget. Tab and Shift+Tab key events are handled automatically
to cycle focus through focusable widgets in depth-first order.

Create a new Manager with [New].

name: Matches
comments: Matches reports whether the shortcut matches the given key event.

name: Shortcut
Biggest
comments:
Biggest returns the biggest finite size that satisfies these constraints.
If a dimension is unbounded (Infinity), it uses the minimum instead.

name: BiggestFinite
signature: func (Constraints) (c Constraints) BiggestFinite(fallbackWidth, fallbackHeight float32) Size
comments: BigggestFinite returns the biggest size, treating Infinity as the provided fallback.

name: BoxConstraints
signature: func BoxConstraints(minWidth, maxWidth, minHeight, maxHeight float32) Constraints
comments:
BoxConstraints creates constraints with explicit min/max dimensions.

Example:

c := geometry.BoxConstraints(50, 200, 30, 100)
// MinWidth=50, MaxWidth=200, MinHeight=30, MaxHeight=100

name: Constrain
comments:
Constrain returns a size that satisfies these constraints.
The returned size will be clamped to [min, max] for each dimension.

Example:

c := geometry.BoxConstraints(50, 200, 30, 100)
s := c.Constrain(geometry.Sz(300, 150)) // Size{200, 100}

name: ConstrainDimensions
signature: func (Constraints) (c Constraints) ConstrainDimensions(width, height float32) (float32, float32)
comments: ConstrainDimensions returns dimensions that satisfy these constraints.

name: ConstrainHeight
comments: ConstrainHeight returns a height that satisfies these constraints.

name: ConstrainWidth
comments: ConstrainWidth returns a width that satisfies these constraints.

name: Deflate
comments:
Deflate returns constraints reduced by the given insets.
This is useful when calculating available space for content inside padding.

Example:

c := geometry.Tight(geometry.Sz(100, 100))
padding := geometry.UniformInsets(10)
content := c.Deflate(padding) // MaxWidth=80, MaxHeight=80

name: Enforce
comments:
Enforce returns constraints that are at least as restrictive as both c and other.
The result has the max of minimums and min of maximums.

name: Expand
comments:
Expand creates constraints where the widget should expand to fill available space.
This is a loose constraint with infinite max dimensions.

Example:

c := geometry.Expand()
// MinWidth=0, MaxWidth=Infinity, MinHeight=0, MaxHeight=Infinity

name: ExpandHeight
comments: ExpandHeight creates constraints that expand vertically but are flexible horizontally.

name: ExpandWidth
comments: ExpandWidth creates constraints that expand horizontally but are flexible vertically.

name: HasBoundedHeight
comments: HasBoundedHeight returns true if max height is not Infinity.

name: HasBoundedWidth
comments: HasBoundedWidth returns true if max width is not Infinity.

name: HasInfiniteHeight
comments: HasInfiniteHeight returns true if max height is Infinity.

name: HasInfiniteWidth
comments: HasInfiniteWidth returns true if max width is Infinity.

name: IsNaN
comments: IsNaN returns true if any value is NaN.

name: IsNormalized
comments: IsNormalized returns true if the constraints are valid (min <= max, no negatives).

name: IsSatisfiedBy
comments:
IsSatisfiedBy returns true if the given size satisfies these constraints.

Example:

c := geometry.BoxConstraints(50, 200, 30, 100)
c.IsSatisfiedBy(geometry.Sz(100, 50)) // true
c.IsSatisfiedBy(geometry.Sz(300, 50)) // false (width too large)

name: IsTight
comments:
IsTight returns true if min equals max for both dimensions.
A tight constraint forces a specific size.

name: IsTightHeight
comments: IsTightHeight returns true if min height equals max height.

name: IsTightWidth
comments: IsTightWidth returns true if min width equals max width.

name: IsUnbounded
comments:
IsUnbounded returns true if both max dimensions are Infinity.
An unbounded constraint has no upper size limit.

name: IsZero
comments: IsZero returns true if all constraints are zero.

name: Loose
comments:
Loose creates constraints where the widget can be any size up to the given size.

Example:

c := geometry.Loose(geometry.Sz(100, 50))
// MinWidth=0, MaxWidth=100, MinHeight=0, MaxHeight=50

name: Loosen
comments:
Loosen returns constraints with the same max but min set to 0.
This allows a child to be smaller than the parent's minimum.

Example:

c := geometry.BoxConstraints(100, 200, 50, 100)
loose := c.Loosen() // MinWidth=0, MaxWidth=200, MinHeight=0, MaxHeight=100

name: LoosenHeight
comments: LoosenHeight returns constraints with min height set to 0.

name: LoosenWidth
comments: LoosenWidth returns constraints with min width set to 0.

name: Normalize
comments:
Normalize returns constraints with mins clamped to not exceed maxes,
and ensures no negative values.

Example:

c := geometry.BoxConstraints(200, 100, 50, 30) // Invalid: min > max
normalized := c.Normalize() // MinWidth=100, MaxWidth=100, MinHeight=30, MaxHeight=30

name: Sanitize
comments:
Sanitize returns constraints with NaN values replaced by appropriate defaults
(0 for minimums, Infinity for maximums).

name: Smallest
comments: Smallest returns the smallest size that satisfies these constraints.

name: String
comments:
String returns a string representation of the constraints.

Example:

c := geometry.BoxConstraints(50, 200, 30, 100)
s := c.String() // "Constraints(50<=w<=200, 30<=h<=100)"

name: Tight
comments:
Tight creates constraints where the widget must be exactly the given size.

Example:

c := geometry.Tight(geometry.Sz(100, 50))
// MinWidth=100, MaxWidth=100, MinHeight=50, MaxHeight=50

name: TightHeight
comments: TightHeight creates constraints with exact height but flexible width.

name: TightWidth
comments: TightWidth creates constraints with exact width but flexible height.

name: Tighten
comments:
Tighten returns tight constraints using the given size, clamped to current constraints.
This is useful when a widget wants to report its preferred size while respecting parent constraints.

Example:

c := geometry.BoxConstraints(50, 200, 30, 100)
tight := c.Tighten(geometry.Sz(150, 80))
// MinWidth=150, MaxWidth=150, MinHeight=80, MaxHeight=80

name: TightenHeight
comments: TightenHeight returns constraints with tight height, keeping width constraints.

name: TightenWidth
comments: TightenWidth returns constraints with tight width, keeping height constraints.

name: Constraints
comments:
Constraints represents box constraints for layout, similar to Flutter's BoxConstraints.

Constraints define the minimum and maximum dimensions a widget can have.
They are passed down the widget tree during layout and used to constrain
the size of child widgets.

A constraint is considered "tight" when min equals max (widget must be exactly that size).
A constraint is "loose" when min is 0 (widget can be any size up to max).
A constraint is "unbounded" when max is Infinity (no upper limit).

The zero value represents unconstrained (0 to Infinity on both dimensions).

name: Abs
comments: Abs returns insets with all values converted to absolute values.

name: Add
comments:
Add returns new insets with values added.

Example:

i1 := geometry.UniformInsets(10)
i2 := geometry.UniformInsets(5)
result := i1.Add(i2) // Insets{15, 15, 15, 15}

name: BottomRight
comments: BottomRight returns the bottom-right offset as a Point.

name: Clamp
signature: func (Insets) (i Insets) Clamp(minInsets, maxInsets Insets) Insets
comments: Clamp returns insets with values clamped to the range [minInsets, maxInsets].

name: Horizontal
comments:
Horizontal returns the sum of left and right insets.

Example:

padding := geometry.UniformInsets(16)
h := padding.Horizontal() // 32

name: InsetsLTRB
signature: func InsetsLTRB(left, top, right, bottom float32) Insets

name: InsetsOnly
signature: func InsetsOnly(top, right, bottom, left float32) Insets
comments:
InsetsOnly creates insets with specific edges set, others zero.

Example:

topPadding := geometry.InsetsOnly(10, 0, 0, 0) // top only

name: InsetsTRBL
signature: func InsetsTRBL(top, right, bottom, left float32) Insets

name: IsNaN
comments: IsNaN returns true if any value is NaN.

name: IsNonNegative
comments: IsNonNegative returns true if all values are >= 0.

name: IsSymmetric
comments: IsSymmetric returns true if horizontal edges match and vertical edges match.

name: IsUniform
comments: IsUniform returns true if all edges have the same value.

name: IsZero
comments: IsZero returns true if all inset values are zero.

name: Max
comments: Max returns insets with the maximum values from i and other.

name: Min
comments: Min returns insets with the minimum values from i and other.

name: Negate
comments: Negate returns insets with all values negated.

name: Sanitize
comments: Sanitize returns a copy with NaN values replaced by zero.

name: Scale
comments:
Scale returns new insets with all values multiplied by the scalar.

Example:

padding := geometry.UniformInsets(10)
doubled := padding.Scale(2) // Insets{20, 20, 20, 20}

name: Size
comments:
Size returns a Size representing the total horizontal and vertical insets.
This is useful for calculating how much space insets consume.

Example:

padding := geometry.SymmetricInsets(16, 8)
s := padding.Size() // Size{Width: 32, Height: 16}

name: String
comments:
String returns a string representation of the insets.

Example:

i := geometry.UniformInsets(16)
s := i.String() // "Insets(16, 16, 16, 16)"

name: Sub
comments: Sub returns new insets with values subtracted.

name: SymmetricInsets
TopLeft
comments: TopLeft returns the top-left offset as a Point.

name: UniformInsets
Vertical
comments:
Vertical returns the sum of top and bottom insets.

Example:

padding := geometry.UniformInsets(16)
v := padding.Vertical() // 32

name: Insets
comments:
Insets represents edge insets for padding, margins, or borders.

Insets define spacing on each of the four edges of a rectangle.
They are commonly used for padding (space inside a widget) and
margins (space outside a widget).

The zero value represents no insets (0 on all edges).

name: Add
comments:
Add returns a new point with the coordinates of p added to other.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(10, 20)
p2 := geometry.Pt(5, 5)
result := p1.Add(p2) // Point{15, 25}

name: Clamp
signature: func (Point) (p Point) Clamp(minP, maxP Point) Point
comments:
Clamp returns a new point with coordinates clamped to the range [minP, maxP].

Example:

p := geometry.Pt(15, -5)
minP := geometry.Pt(0, 0)
maxP := geometry.Pt(10, 10)
result := p.Clamp(minP, maxP) // Point{10, 0}

name: Distance
comments:
Distance returns the Euclidean distance between p and other.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(0, 0)
p2 := geometry.Pt(3, 4)
d := p1.Distance(p2) // 5.0

name: DistanceSquared
comments:
DistanceSquared returns the squared Euclidean distance between p and other.
This is faster than Distance when only comparing distances.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(0, 0)
p2 := geometry.Pt(3, 4)
d2 := p1.DistanceSquared(p2) // 25.0

name: Div
comments:
Div returns a new point with coordinates divided component-wise.
If a component of other is zero, the result for that component is zero.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(10, 20)
p2 := geometry.Pt(2, 4)
result := p1.Div(p2) // Point{5, 5}

name: Dot
comments:
Dot returns the dot product of p and other.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(1, 2)
p2 := geometry.Pt(3, 4)
d := p1.Dot(p2) // 11.0 (1*3 + 2*4)

name: IsNaN
comments: IsNaN returns true if either coordinate is NaN.

name: IsZero
comments: IsZero returns true if both coordinates are zero.

name: Length
comments:
Length returns the length (magnitude) of the vector from origin to p.

Example:

p := geometry.Pt(3, 4)
l := p.Length() // 5.0

name: LengthSquared
comments:
LengthSquared returns the squared length of the vector from origin to p.
This is faster than Length when only comparing lengths.

name: Lerp
signature: func (Point) (p Point) Lerp(other Point, t float32) Point
comments:
Lerp returns a point linearly interpolated between p and other.
t=0 returns p, t=1 returns other, values outside [0,1] extrapolate.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(0, 0)
p2 := geometry.Pt(10, 20)
mid := p1.Lerp(p2, 0.5) // Point{5, 10}

name: Max
comments:
Max returns a new point with the maximum coordinates of p and other.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(10, 5)
p2 := geometry.Pt(3, 20)
result := p1.Max(p2) // Point{10, 20}

name: Min
comments:
Min returns a new point with the minimum coordinates of p and other.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(10, 5)
p2 := geometry.Pt(3, 20)
result := p1.Min(p2) // Point{3, 5}

name: Mul
comments:
Mul returns a new point with coordinates multiplied component-wise.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(10, 20)
p2 := geometry.Pt(2, 3)
result := p1.Mul(p2) // Point{20, 60}

name: Negate
comments:
Negate returns a new point with both coordinates negated.

Example:

p := geometry.Pt(10, -20)
result := p.Negate() // Point{-10, 20}

name: Normalize
comments:
Normalize returns a unit vector in the same direction as p.
If p is the zero point, returns the zero point.

Example:

p := geometry.Pt(3, 4)
n := p.Normalize() // Point{0.6, 0.8}

name: Pt
comments:
Pt is a shorthand constructor for creating a Point.

Example:

p := geometry.Pt(10, 20)

name: Sanitize
comments: Sanitize returns a copy of p with NaN values replaced by zero.

name: Scale
comments:
Scale returns a new point with both coordinates multiplied by the scalar.

Example:

p := geometry.Pt(10, 20)
result := p.Scale(2) // Point{20, 40}

name: String
comments:
String returns a string representation of the point.

Example:

p := geometry.Pt(10.5, 20.25)
s := p.String() // "Point(10.5, 20.25)"

name: Sub
comments:
Sub returns a new point with the coordinates of other subtracted from p.

Example:

p1 := geometry.Pt(10, 20)
p2 := geometry.Pt(3, 5)
result := p1.Sub(p2) // Point{7, 15}

name: Point
comments:
Point represents a 2D point with float32 coordinates.

Point uses float32 for GPU compatibility and efficient memory layout.
All operations return new values without modifying the original point.

The zero value is the origin point (0, 0).

name: Area
comments:
Area returns the area of the rectangle.
Returns 0 for empty rectangles.

name: BottomLeft
comments: BottomLeft returns the bottom-left corner.

name: BottomRight
comments: BottomRight returns the bottom-right corner (same as Max).

name: Center
comments:
Center returns the center point of the rectangle.

Example:

r := geometry.NewRect(0, 0, 100, 50)
c := r.Center() // Point{50, 25}

name: Contains
comments:
Contains returns true if the point p is inside or on the edge of the rectangle.

Example:

r := geometry.NewRect(0, 0, 100, 50)
r.Contains(geometry.Pt(50, 25)) // true
r.Contains(geometry.Pt(150, 25)) // false

name: ContainsRect
comments:
ContainsRect returns true if other is entirely inside or equal to r.

Example:

outer := geometry.NewRect(0, 0, 100, 100)
inner := geometry.NewRect(10, 10, 50, 50)
outer.ContainsRect(inner) // true

name: Expand
comments:
Expand returns a new rectangle with all edges moved outward by delta.
Negative delta values shrink the rectangle.

Example:

r := geometry.NewRect(10, 10, 80, 80)
expanded := r.Expand(5) // Rect{Min:(5,5), Max:(95,95)}

name: FromCenter
signature: func FromCenter(center Point, s Size) Rect
comments:
FromCenter creates a rectangle centered at the given point with the given size.

Example:

r := geometry.FromCenter(geometry.Pt(50, 50), geometry.Sz(100, 50))
// Min: (0, 25), Max: (100, 75)

name: FromMinMax
comments:
FromMinMax creates a rectangle from two corner points.
The points are normalized so Min contains the smaller coordinates.

name: FromPointSize
signature: func FromPointSize(p Point, s Size) Rect
comments:
FromPointSize creates a rectangle from a point (top-left) and size.

Example:

r := geometry.FromPointSize(geometry.Pt(10, 20), geometry.Sz(100, 50))

name: Height
comments: Height returns the height of the rectangle.

name: Inset
comments:
Inset returns a new rectangle with edges moved inward by the specified insets.
Positive inset values shrink the rectangle, negative values expand it.

Example:

r := geometry.NewRect(0, 0, 100, 100)
padding := geometry.UniformInsets(10)
inner := r.Inset(padding) // Rect{Min:(10,10), Max:(90,90)}

name: Intersection
comments:
Intersection returns the overlapping area of r and other.
If the rectangles don't overlap, returns an empty rectangle.

Example:

r1 := geometry.NewRect(0, 0, 100, 100)
r2 := geometry.NewRect(50, 50, 100, 100)
inter := r1.Intersection(r2) // Rect{Min:(50,50), Max:(100,100)}

name: Intersects
comments:
Intersects returns true if r and other overlap (share any area).

Example:

r1 := geometry.NewRect(0, 0, 100, 100)
r2 := geometry.NewRect(50, 50, 100, 100)
r1.Intersects(r2) // true

name: IsEmpty
comments:
IsEmpty returns true if the rectangle has zero or negative area.
This can happen when Min >= Max in either dimension.

name: IsNaN
comments: IsNaN returns true if any coordinate is NaN.

name: IsZero
comments: IsZero returns true if the rectangle is the zero value.

name: NewRect
signature: func NewRect(x, y, width, height float32) Rect
comments:
NewRect creates a rectangle from position (x, y) and dimensions (w, h).

Example:

r := geometry.NewRect(10, 20, 100, 50)
// Min: (10, 20), Max: (110, 70)

name: Normalize
comments:
Normalize returns a copy of r with Min and Max swapped if necessary
so that Min contains the smaller coordinates.

name: Sanitize
comments: Sanitize returns a copy of r with NaN values replaced by zero.

name: Size
comments:
Size returns the dimensions of the rectangle.

Example:

r := geometry.NewRect(10, 20, 100, 50)
s := r.Size() // Size{100, 50}

name: String
comments:
String returns a string representation of the rectangle.

Example:

r := geometry.NewRect(10, 20, 100, 50)
str := r.String() // "Rect(10, 20, 100x50)"

name: TopLeft
comments: TopLeft returns the top-left corner (same as Min).

name: TopRight
comments: TopRight returns the top-right corner.

name: Translate
TranslateXY
signature: func (Rect) (r Rect) TranslateXY(dx, dy float32) Rect
comments: TranslateXY returns a new rectangle moved by (dx, dy).

name: Union
comments:
Union returns the smallest rectangle containing both r and other.

Example:

r1 := geometry.NewRect(0, 0, 50, 50)
r2 := geometry.NewRect(100, 100, 50, 50)
union := r1.Union(r2) // Rect{Min:(0,0), Max:(150,150)}

name: Width
comments: Width returns the width of the rectangle.

name: WithCenter
comments: WithCenter returns a new rectangle with the same size but centered at the given point.

name: WithSize
comments: WithSize returns a new rectangle with the same Min point but different size.

name: Rect
comments:
Rect represents an axis-aligned rectangle defined by its minimum and maximum corners.

A rectangle is considered valid when Min.X <= Max.X and Min.Y <= Max.Y.
Some operations may return invalid rectangles (e.g., Intersection when
rectangles don't overlap). Use IsEmpty() to check validity.

The zero value is an empty rectangle at the origin.

name: Add
comments:
Add returns a new size with dimensions added.

Example:

s1 := geometry.Sz(100, 50)
s2 := geometry.Sz(10, 20)
result := s1.Add(s2) // Size{110, 70}

name: Area
comments:
Area returns the area (Width * Height).
Returns negative value if one dimension is negative.

Example:

s := geometry.Sz(100, 50)
area := s.Area() // 5000

name: AspectRatio
comments:
AspectRatio returns Width / Height.
Returns 0 if Height is zero.

name: Clamp
signature: func (Size) (s Size) Clamp(minSize, maxSize Size) Size
comments:
Clamp returns a new size with dimensions clamped to the range [minSize, maxSize].

Example:

s := geometry.Sz(150, 25)
minS := geometry.Sz(50, 50)
maxS := geometry.Sz(100, 100)
result := s.Clamp(minS, maxS) // Size{100, 50}

name: Contains
comments:
Contains returns true if s can contain other.
Both dimensions of s must be >= corresponding dimensions of other.

Example:

s1 := geometry.Sz(100, 50)
s2 := geometry.Sz(80, 40)
s1.Contains(s2) // true

name: Contract
comments:
Contract returns a new size with dimensions decreased by delta on each edge.
Total decrease is 2*delta for each dimension.

Example:

s := geometry.Sz(100, 50)
result := s.Contract(10) // Size{80, 30}

name: Expand
comments:
Expand returns a new size with dimensions increased by delta on each edge.
Total increase is 2*delta for each dimension.

Example:

s := geometry.Sz(100, 50)
result := s.Expand(10) // Size{120, 70}

name: FillIn
comments:
FillIn returns a size that maintains aspect ratio while filling maxSize.
The resulting size will have at least one dimension equal to maxSize,
and will completely cover maxSize (may overflow in one dimension).

Example:

s := geometry.Sz(200, 100)     // 2:1 aspect ratio
maxS := geometry.Sz(100, 100)
result := s.FillIn(maxS)       // Size{200, 100}

name: FitIn
comments:
FitIn returns a size that maintains aspect ratio while fitting within maxSize.
If the size already fits within maxSize, it is returned unchanged.
Otherwise, the size is scaled down proportionally.

Example:

s := geometry.Sz(200, 100)     // 2:1 aspect ratio
maxS := geometry.Sz(100, 100)
result := s.FitIn(maxS)        // Size{100, 50}

name: IsEmpty
comments:
IsEmpty returns true if either dimension is zero or negative.

Example:

geometry.Sz(100, 50).IsEmpty() // false
geometry.Sz(100, 0).IsEmpty()  // true
geometry.Sz(-1, 50).IsEmpty()  // true

name: IsNaN
comments: IsNaN returns true if either dimension is NaN.

name: IsZero
comments: IsZero returns true if both dimensions are zero.

name: Max
comments:
Max returns a new size with the maximum dimensions of s and other.

Example:

s1 := geometry.Sz(100, 30)
s2 := geometry.Sz(80, 50)
result := s1.Max(s2) // Size{100, 50}

name: Min
comments:
Min returns a new size with the minimum dimensions of s and other.

Example:

s1 := geometry.Sz(100, 30)
s2 := geometry.Sz(80, 50)
result := s1.Min(s2) // Size{80, 30}

name: Sanitize
comments: Sanitize returns a copy of s with NaN values replaced by zero.

name: Scale
comments:
Scale returns a new size with both dimensions multiplied by the scalar.

Example:

s := geometry.Sz(100, 50)
result := s.Scale(2) // Size{200, 100}

name: String
comments:
String returns a string representation of the size.

Example:

s := geometry.Sz(100, 50)
str := s.String() // "Size(100, 50)"

name: Sub
comments:
Sub returns a new size with dimensions subtracted.

Example:

s1 := geometry.Sz(100, 50)
s2 := geometry.Sz(10, 20)
result := s1.Sub(s2) // Size{90, 30}

name: Sz
comments:
Sz is a shorthand constructor for creating a Size.

Example:

s := geometry.Sz(100, 50)

name: ToPoint
comments:
ToPoint converts the size to a point (Width -> X, Height -> Y).
Useful for offset calculations.

name: Size
comments:
Size represents dimensions with Width and Height.

Size uses float32 for GPU compatibility. Negative dimensions are allowed
but may have special meaning in some contexts (e.g., "shrink to fit").

The zero value represents empty dimensions (0x0).

name: Get
comments:
Get retrieves a simple message by key.

Returns the message and true if found, or empty string and false if not.

name: GetPlural
comments:
GetPlural retrieves plural forms by key.

Returns the forms and true if found, or zero PluralForms and false if not.

name: Keys
comments: Keys returns all message keys (both simple and plural) in no particular order.

name: Len
comments: Len returns the total number of messages (simple + plural keys).

name: Locale
comments: Locale returns the locale this bundle is for.

name: NewBundle
comments: NewBundle creates a new empty Bundle for the given locale.

name: Set
comments: Set adds or replaces a simple message for the given key.

name: SetAll
comments:
SetAll copies all messages from another bundle into this one.

Existing keys are overwritten. This is useful for merging partial
translations with a base bundle.

name: SetPlural
comments: SetPlural adds or replaces plural forms for the given key.

name: Bundle
comments:
Bundle is a message catalog for a single locale.

A Bundle holds key-value message pairs and optional plural forms for a
specific locale. Bundles are NOT thread-safe; they should be fully
populated before being added to a [Translator].

Example:

en := i18n.NewBundle(i18n.NewLocale("en", "US"))
en.Set("welcome", "Welcome!")
en.SetPlural("files", i18n.PluralForms{
One:   "%d file",
Other: "%d files",
})

name: DirectionForLanguage
comments:
DirectionForLanguage returns the text direction for the given ISO 639-1
language code.

Returns [RTL] for Arabic, Hebrew, Persian, Urdu, and other RTL languages.
Returns [LTR] for all other languages.

name: IsRTL
comments: IsRTL returns true if the direction is right-to-left.

name: String
comments: String returns the human-readable name of the direction.

name: Direction
comments:
Direction returns the text direction for this locale.

Returns [RTL] for Arabic ("ar"), Hebrew ("he"), Persian ("fa"),
and Urdu ("ur"). Returns [LTR] for all other languages.

name: IsZero
comments: IsZero returns true if the locale has no language set.

name: Matches
comments:
Matches reports whether this locale matches the other locale.

A locale with an empty region matches any locale with the same language.
Both language comparisons are case-insensitive.

name: NewLocale
comments:
NewLocale creates a new Locale with the given language and region.

Language is normalized to lowercase, region to uppercase, following
BCP 47 conventions. If region is empty, the locale matches any region
for that language.

Example:

en := i18n.NewLocale("en", "US")  // English (United States)
ru := i18n.NewLocale("ru", "")    // Russian (any region)

name: ParseLocale
String
comments:
String returns the locale in "language-REGION" format (e.g., "en-US").

If Region is empty, returns just the language (e.g., "en").

name: Locale
comments:
Locale represents a language and optional region combination.

Language codes follow BCP 47 / ISO 639-1 (e.g., "en", "ru", "ar").
Region codes follow ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 (e.g., "US", "RU", "SA").

A Locale with an empty Region matches any region for that language
during fallback resolution.

name: Get
comments:
Get returns the message string for the given plural category.

If the requested category has an empty string, falls back to Other.
code:
func (p PluralForms) Get(cat PluralCategory) string {
	var s string

	switch cat {
	case PluralZero:
		s = p.Zero
	case PluralOne:
		s = p.One
	case PluralTwo:
		s = p.Two
	case PluralFew:
		s = p.Few
	case PluralMany:
		s = p.Many
	case PluralOther:
		s = p.Other
	}

	if s == "" {
		return p.Other
	}

	return s
}

name: PluralRuleArabic
comments:
PluralRuleArabic implements CLDR plural rules for Arabic.

Categories:
- zero: n=0
- one: n=1
- two: n=2
- few: n%100 in 3..10
- many: n%100 in 11..99
- other: everything else (100, 200, ...)
code:
func PluralRuleArabic(count int) PluralCategory {
	n := abs(count)
	mod100 := n % 100

	switch {
	case n == 0:
		return PluralZero
	case n == 1:
		return PluralOne
	case n == 2:
		return PluralTwo
	case mod100 >= 3 && mod100 <= 10:
		return PluralFew
	case mod100 >= 11 && mod100 <= 99:
		return PluralMany
	default:
		return PluralOther
	}
}

name: PluralRuleEnglish
comments:
PluralRuleEnglish implements CLDR plural rules for English.

Categories: one (n=1), other (everything else).

name: PluralRuleFrench
comments:
PluralRuleFrench implements CLDR plural rules for French and
other Romance languages that treat 0 as singular.

Categories: one (n=0 or n=1), other (everything else).

name: PluralRuleJapanese
comments:
PluralRuleJapanese implements CLDR plural rules for Japanese, Chinese,
Korean, Thai, and other languages with no grammatical plural.

Categories: other (always).

name: PluralRulePolish
comments:
PluralRulePolish implements CLDR plural rules for Polish.

Categories:
- one: n=1
- few: n%10 in 2..4 and n%100 not in 12..14
- many: everything else

name: PluralRuleRussian
comments:
PluralRuleRussian implements CLDR plural rules for Russian and other
Slavic languages (Ukrainian, Belarusian, Serbian, Croatian).

Categories:
- one: n%10=1 and n%100!=11 (1, 21, 31, 41...)
- few: n%10 in 2..4 and n%100 not in 12..14 (2-4, 22-24, 32-34...)
- many: n%10=0 or n%10 in 5..9 or n%100 in 11..14 (0, 5-20, 25-30...)
- other: fallback (non-integer, but we handle int only)

name: PluralForms
comments:
PluralForms holds message strings for each CLDR plural category.

Not all categories are used by every language. For example, English only
uses One and Other, while Arabic uses all six categories. When a category
is not set (empty string), the translator falls back to Other.

Example (English):

PluralForms{One: "%d item", Other: "%d items"}

Example (Russian):

PluralForms{
One:   "%d файл",    // 1, 21, 31...
Few:   "%d файла",   // 2-4, 22-24...
Many:  "%d файлов",  // 5-20, 25-30...
Other: "%d файлов",  // fallback
}

name: AddBundle
comments:
AddBundle registers a message bundle for its locale.

If a bundle for the same locale string already exists, it is replaced.
Bundles should be fully populated before being added.

name: BundleCount
comments: BundleCount returns the number of registered bundles.

name: Direction
comments: Direction returns the text direction for the current locale.

name: Fallback
comments: Fallback returns the fallback locale.

name: Has
comments:
Has reports whether a message with the given key exists in the current
or fallback locale.

name: Locale
comments: Locale returns the current locale.

name: LocaleSignal
NewTranslator
comments:
NewTranslator creates a new Translator with the given fallback locale.

The fallback locale is used when a message is not found in the current locale.
The current locale is initially set to the fallback.

name: SetFallback
comments: SetFallback changes the fallback locale.

name: SetLocale
comments:
SetLocale changes the current locale.

This triggers the locale signal, notifying all subscribers.

name: SetPluralRule
comments:
SetPluralRule registers a custom plural rule for a language.

This overrides the built-in CLDR rule for the given language code.

name: T
comments:
T resolves a simple message by key.

Resolution order: current locale -> fallback locale -> key itself.

name: Tf
comments:
Tf resolves a message by key and formats it with fmt.Sprintf.

Resolution order: current locale -> fallback locale -> key itself.

Example:

t.Tf("greeting.name", "World")  // "Hello, World!"

name: Tp
signature: func (*Translator) (t *Translator) Tp(key string, count int) string
comments:
Tp resolves a plural message by key and count.

The plural category is determined by the locale's plural rules,
then the appropriate plural form is selected and formatted with
the count value.

Example:

t.Tp("items", 1)   // "1 item"
t.Tp("items", 5)   // "5 items"

name: Tpf
signature: func (*Translator) (t *Translator) Tpf(key string, count int, args ...any) string

name: Translator
comments:
Translator resolves localized messages with fallback chain support.

The resolution order for a message key is:
1. Current locale (exact match: language + region)
2. Current locale (language-only match)
3. Fallback locale (exact match)
4. Fallback locale (language-only match)
5. The key itself (as a last resort)

Translator is safe for concurrent access from multiple goroutines.

Example:

t := i18n.NewTranslator(i18n.NewLocale("en", "US"))
t.AddBundle(enBundle)
t.AddBundle(ruBundle)

t.T("greeting")  // resolves from en-US bundle
t.SetLocale(i18n.NewLocale("ru", "RU"))
t.T("greeting")  // resolves from ru-RU bundle

name: Draw
signature: func Draw(canvas widget.Canvas, data IconData, bounds geometry.Rect, color widget.Color)
comments:
Draw renders an icon's path operations onto the canvas within the given
bounds, using the specified color.

The icon is uniformly scaled to fit the bounds while preserving aspect ratio
(the viewbox is square). The stroke width scales proportionally.

Draw can be called directly for custom rendering, or is used internally by
[IconWidget].

name: DrawMulti
signature: func DrawMulti(canvas widget.Canvas, data MultiColorIcon, bounds geometry.Rect, palette Palette)
comments:
DrawMulti renders a multi-color icon onto the canvas within the given bounds.

Each [PathGroup] in the icon is drawn with the color mapped by its ColorKey
in the palette. If a key is not found in the palette, the group is drawn
with [widget.ColorGray] as a fallback.

name: ClosePath
comments: ClosePath creates a Close path operation.

name: Cubic
signature: func Cubic(cx1, cy1, cx2, cy2, x, y float32) PathOp
comments:
Cubic creates a CubicTo path operation with control points (cx1, cy1),
(cx2, cy2) and endpoint (x, y).

name: Line
comments: Line creates a LineTo path operation.

name: Move
comments: Move creates a MoveTo path operation.

name: Quad
signature: func Quad(cx, cy, x, y float32) PathOp
comments:
Quad creates a QuadraticTo path operation with control point (cx, cy)
and endpoint (x, y).

name: String
comments: String returns a human-readable name for the command.

name: PathOp
comments:
PathOp is a single drawing operation in an icon's path definition.

The number of significant parameters depends on the command:
- [CmdMoveTo]: 2 (x, y)
- [CmdLineTo]: 2 (x, y)
- [CmdCubicTo]: 6 (cx1, cy1, cx2, cy2, x, y)
- [CmdQuadraticTo]: 4 (cx, cy, x, y)
- [CmdClose]: 0

name: IconData
comments:
IconData defines a vector icon as a sequence of path operations within a
square viewbox.

IconData is a value type: it is safe to copy, compare by name, and store
in maps. The Ops slice is shared between copies; callers must not mutate
the slice after constructing the IconData.

name: PathGroup
comments:
PathGroup is a named group of path operations that share a color role.
Multi-color icons contain multiple groups, each rendered with a different
color from a [Palette].

name: MultiColorIcon
comments:
MultiColorIcon defines a vector icon with multiple color groups.
Each group is rendered with a different color from the provided [Palette].

MultiColorIcon is a value type: it is safe to copy and compare by name.
The Groups and their Ops slices are shared between copies; callers must
not mutate them after construction.

name: DefaultDarkPalette
comments:
DefaultDarkPalette returns a palette suitable for dark themes.

The color values are inspired by JetBrains IDE dark themes and provide
good contrast on dark backgrounds.
code:
func DefaultDarkPalette() Palette {
	return Palette{
		KeyPrimary:	widget.Hex(0xDFE1E5),	// Gray12 — default foreground
		KeyAccent:	widget.Hex(0x3574F0),	// Blue6 — primary accent
		KeySecondary:	widget.Hex(0x9DA0A8),	// Gray9
		KeySuccess:	widget.Hex(0x57965C),	// Green6
		KeyError:	widget.Hex(0xDB5C5C),	// Red7
		KeyWarning:	widget.Hex(0xC69026),	// Yellow6
		KeyGo:		widget.Hex(0x00ADD8),	// Go cyan
		KeyJSON:	widget.Hex(0xEDA200),	// Gold
		KeyYAML:	widget.Hex(0x59A869),	// Green
		KeyRust:	widget.Hex(0xDEA584),	// Rust orange
		KeyPython:	widget.Hex(0x3776AB),	// Python blue
		KeyMarkdown:	widget.Hex(0x9DA0A8),	// Gray
	}
}

name: DefaultLightPalette
comments:
DefaultLightPalette returns a palette suitable for light themes.

The color values provide good contrast on light backgrounds with slightly
darker tones than the dark palette counterparts.
code:
func DefaultLightPalette() Palette {
	return Palette{
		KeyPrimary:	widget.Hex(0x3D3F43),	// Dark gray — default foreground
		KeyAccent:	widget.Hex(0x2B5FC3),	// Blue — primary accent
		KeySecondary:	widget.Hex(0x6E7076),	// Medium gray
		KeySuccess:	widget.Hex(0x3B7A40),	// Dark green

name: DefaultMultiColorRegistry
comments:
DefaultMultiColorRegistry returns the global multi-color icon registry.

The default registry is pre-populated with all built-in multi-color icons
(file type icons and VCS icons). Additional icons can be registered at
any time using [MultiColorRegistry.Register].

name: DefaultRegistry
comments:
DefaultRegistry returns the global icon registry.

The default registry is pre-populated with all built-in icons. Additional
icons can be registered at any time using [Registry.Register].

name: Get
comments:
Get returns the icon with the given name and true if found, or a zero
IconData and false otherwise.

name: Get
comments:
Get returns the multi-color icon with the given name and true if found,
or a zero MultiColorIcon and false otherwise.

name: Len
comments: Len returns the number of icons in the registry.

name: Len
comments: Len returns the number of multi-color icons in the registry.

name: Names
comments: Names returns all registered icon names in no particular order.

name: Names
comments: Names returns all registered multi-color icon names in no particular order.

name: NewMultiColorRegistry
comments: NewMultiColorRegistry creates an empty multi-color icon registry.

name: NewRegistry
comments: NewRegistry creates an empty icon registry.

name: Register
comments:
Register adds an icon to the registry, keyed by its Name field.

If an icon with the same name already exists, it is replaced.

name: Register
comments:
Register adds a multi-color icon to the registry, keyed by its Name field.

If an icon with the same name already exists, it is replaced.

name: Registry
comments:
Registry is a thread-safe named icon registry.

Use [DefaultRegistry] to access the global registry, which is pre-populated
with all built-in icons. Create a custom registry with [NewRegistry] for
isolated icon sets.

name: MultiColorRegistry
comments:
MultiColorRegistry is a thread-safe named registry for multi-color icons.

Use [DefaultMultiColorRegistry] to access the global registry, which is
pre-populated with all built-in multi-color icons. Create a custom
registry with [NewMultiColorRegistry] for isolated icon sets.

name: FromSVG
signature: func FromSVG(name string, viewBox float32, svgPathData string) IconData
comments:
FromSVG creates an IconData from an SVG path data string.

The viewBox specifies the SVG coordinate space side length (e.g., 16 for
a 16x16 viewBox, 24 for Material Design's 24x24). SVG path commands
are parsed using [gg.ParseSVGPath] and converted to [PathOp] operations.

FromSVG panics if the SVG path data is invalid. This is intentional because
icon definitions are typically package-level variables initialized at startup;
a malformed path indicates a programming error that should fail fast.

Example:

var MyIcon = icon.FromSVG("my_icon", 16, "M8 2L14 8L8 14L2 8Z")

name: FromSVGStroke
signature: func FromSVGStroke(name string, viewBox float32, svgPathData string) IconData
comments:
FromSVGStroke creates an IconData for stroke-based SVG icons.
These are rendered via stroke (DrawLine) not fill, matching expui outline style.

name: FromSVGXML
comments:
FromSVGXML creates an IconData from full SVG XML data.
The SVG is rendered via gg/svg.RenderWithColor into a bitmap at the
target size, matching JetBrains icon rendering pipeline.
This handles all SVG elements: path, circle, rect, with proper
fill, stroke, fill-rule, stroke-linecap, etc.

name: TryFromSVG
signature: func TryFromSVG(name string, viewBox float32, svgPathData string) (IconData, error)
comments:
TryFromSVG creates an IconData from SVG path data, returning an error
instead of panicking if the data is invalid. This is useful for
user-supplied or runtime-loaded icon data.

name: AccessibilityActions

name: AccessibilityHint

name: AccessibilityLabel

name: AccessibilityRole

name: AccessibilityState

name: AccessibilityValue

name: Children

name: Color

name: ColorSignal

name: Data
comments: Data returns the icon data being displayed.

name: Draw

name: Event

name: IconColor

name: IconLabel

name: IconSize

name: Label

name: Layout

name: Mount

LayoutAlgorithm

name: Name

name: FlexLayout
comments:
FlexLayout implements CSS Flexbox-style layout.

FlexLayout arranges children along a main axis (row or column),
distributing space according to flex properties from the node styles.

# Properties Used

From parent style:
- FlexDirection: main axis direction
- FlexWrap: whether items wrap
- JustifyContent: main axis space distribution
- AlignItems: cross axis alignment
- Gap: space between items

From child styles:
- FlexGrow: how much item grows to fill space
- FlexShrink: how much item shrinks when space is tight
- FlexBasis: initial size before grow/shrink
code: type FlexLayout struct{}

comments: Compute performs grid layout on the tree starting at root.

name: RegisterWithName
